newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma City okays stadium plans, doubts remain.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma City okays stadium plans, doubts remain.

text.p: Oklahoma City's council on Tuesday approved preliminary plans for a $84.5 million sports arena but the project's future remains uncertain after the city's hopes for a National Hockey League franchise faded.
The City Council also authorized officials to draw up final design plans for the arena while it considers whether to proceed with the project.

"The council will look at various options before a final decision is made but right now we have the authorization to proceed with the construction plans," Assistant City Manager Jim Thompson told Reuters in a telephone interview.

The planned sports arena is part of a $300 million Oklahoma City Metropolitan Area Projects program approved by voters in 1993. The projects, some of which are already under way, are being financed by a 1 cent sales tax hike applied over a five-year period.

Oklahoma City was one of six cities that applied for a NHL franchise but the NHL expansion committee last week voted against Oklahoma City and Houston while recommending Atlanta, Nashville, Minneapolis and Columbus, Ohio.
City officials still hope to convince the NHL that it has a large enough population -- 550,000 people -- and sufficient facilities to support an expansion team.
Under current plans, the Oklahoma City sports arena would be used for ice hockey and basketball games as well as concerts for up to 20,000 spectators.
Thompson said about $3.5 million has already been spent on the project for land acquisition and design work but that changes could be made.
"Among options before the council are whether the arena should be built without the hockey franchise," Thompson said.
